limits.resetPolicy: Two reset regimes exist. (1) COST-METERED counters reset periodically: receipt scans and AI/Echo chat calls reset MONTHLY — premiumStore.ts:57-69 (resetScanCountIfNeeded) and :77-89 (resetAiCallsIfNeeded) zero the count when the stored reset date falls before startOfMonth(now); Collectz session CREATIONS reset per CALENDAR WEEK (tiers.ts:26-28, key name maxCollectzSessionsPerWeek). (2) COUNT caps (wallets, wallets-per-type, budgets, savings, goals, shared subs, playbooks) are NOT time-windowed — they are lifetime/concurrent ceilings on how many can exist at once; canCreate() (tiers.ts:116-118) simply blocks the next create and grandfathers anyone already over a lowered cap (never deletes). Chat-history limits (saved/memory/txn-detail bubbles) are structural, not periodic. Capability flags (export, Google Docs sync, cloud backup, Ask Echo, photo icons) are on/off entitlements, not counters. Design principle stated at tiers.ts:10-12: count features go Unlimited at Pro+, but cost-metered features (scans, AI) stay capped even on Premium to protect margin.

echo.whatIsEcho: Echo is Potraces's built-in AI assistant — a Gemini-powered chat "friend" that can see all the user's financial data (spending, wallets, debts, goals, subscriptions, playbooks, savings) and answer money questions in a calm, non-judgmental, Malaysian tone. It can also PREPARE money entries (expenses, income, debts, splits, transfers, etc.) as tap-to-confirm chips, but it never saves anything itself — the owner must tap to confirm. Source: src/services/moneyChat.ts:1-7 (module header "Echo — Gemini-powered conversational AI"), :38-39 (system prompt "You are Echo, the AI inside Potraces"), :66-74 (confirmation model — Echo cannot save/edit/delete on its own). Echo can also ANSWER with rich data CARDS — a visual card showing the exact figures for a money question (spending, wallet balance, bills, subscriptions, debts, goals, savings, budgets, net worth, biggest spends, top merchants, and more). The AI only chooses WHICH card fits the question; the app fills every number from the user's own data (never the AI), so the figures are always accurate — this is free on ALL tiers, not gated. Source: src/services/echoCards/* (parse/builders/select/fillCards) + src/components/common/EchoCardView.tsx, attached in MoneyChat.tsx processResponse.

echo.howChatsAreCounted: Counted PER MESSAGE/REPLY, not per conversation. premiumStore.incrementAiCalls() is called exactly once after each successful Echo reply — src/services/moneyChat.ts:1030 (non-streaming path) and :1100 (streaming path), both right after a non-empty reply text is returned. A message that fails, is rate-limited, or returns empty does NOT increment. Each queued/sent message that gets answered counts as 1; an image message also counts as 1. IMPORTANT: this 30/mo counter (aiCallsCount) is a SHARED monthly AI pool, not Echo-chat-only — other AI features also call incrementAiCalls() against it: collectzParser.ts:111, intentEngine.ts:507, playbookAI.ts:628/729/777, queryEngine.ts:397. The opt-in daily check-in is excluded: it checks canUseAI() headroom (checkinMessage.ts:29) but never increments, so it 'doesn't spend the chat quota' (MoneyChat.tsx:1262-1263).
echo.whenChatsReset: Monthly, at the start of each calendar month. resetAiCallsIfNeeded() (src/store/premiumStore.ts:77-89) resets aiCallsCount to 0 whenever the stored aiCallsResetDate is before startOfMonth(now); it's lazily triggered on the next AI activity (canUseAI/incrementAiCalls) in the new month. Reset date is initialized to startOfMonth (premiumStore.ts:34). The user-facing error even says 'Resets next month!' (moneyChat.ts:921).
echo.afterLimit: Soft block, not a hard modal paywall. When the free user is out of calls, the send is stopped at the pre-flight gate: _preflightGate() calls usePremiumStore.canUseAI() (moneyChat.ts:920) which returns false, so the send returns { ok:false, error:'AI limit reached this month. Resets next month!' } (moneyChat.ts:920-922; canUseAI in premiumStore.ts:109-112). In the chat screen, result.ok is false so showError(result.error) runs (MoneyChat.tsx:1958-1962), which displays that string as a calm inline error banner that auto-dismisses after ~4 seconds (MoneyChat.tsx:1294-1298). The user's typed message still appears as their bubble but gets no Echo reply. It is NOT degraded to a weaker answer and does NOT pop a purchase modal in the main chat — you simply get no response until next month or upgrade. (The PaywallModal at MoneyChat.tsx:2647-2657 is unrelated: it gates the saved-chat-HISTORY cap chatSavedBubbles, not the monthly call limit.) Separately, on the 5 secondary screens the Echo FAB itself is paywalled for free users via askEchoPerScreen (EchoFab.tsx:171).
echo.smartAiByTier: Yes — Echo is genuinely smarter on paying tiers, in two ways. (1) Model: chatModelForTier() (src/services/chatModel.ts:23-25) gives Pro/Premium the smart model CHAT_MODEL_SMART='gemini-3.5-flash' and Free/Basic the cheaper CHAT_MODEL_LITE='gemini-3.1-flash-lite' (chatModel.ts:15-16). hasSmartAi(tier) is true only for 'pro'/'premium' (chatModel.ts:28-30) and drives the 'smarter AI' paywall copy. The chosen model is passed into the Gemini call at moneyChat.ts:1013 and :1087 (with a 429 fallback down the chain). (2) Context depth also scales by tier: chatMemoryBubbles (recent bubbles re-sent to the model each reply) = Free 15 / Basic 30 / Pro 45 / Premium 90, and chatTxnDetail (per-line transactions Echo sees) = Free 30 / Basic 100 / Pro 500 / Premium 500 (tiers.ts:58,68,78,88; used at moneyChat.ts:961 and :505). So higher tiers get a better model AND more memory/data.
echo.otherNotes: Free users effectively can only chat with Echo from the dedicated Money Chat screen; the floating Echo button on Budget/Pulse/Savings/Subscriptions/Wallet is locked for them (askEchoPerScreen:false, tiers.ts:60) and opens the paywall. Note the metered AI cap stays finite even at Premium (1500/mo) by design — cost-metered features never go unlimited (tiers.ts:9-12,29-31). The reset is monthly for AI calls (there is no daily-chat concept); the only daily concept is the optional check-in greeting, which doesn't consume the quota. ECHO'S NOTEBOOK (added 2026-07-28): Echo's per-user 'memory' is a local learning store (src/store/learningStore.ts + learningPure.ts), NOT AI training — four capped tables (category / person-alias / wallet / type-correction, max 100 entries each, lowest-count eviction) filled from the user's own corrections in ~10 spots (receipt review, chat edits, transaction edits, quick add, notes). A rule is only trusted at count≥2, so one accident can't poison it; correcting a rule demotes it (-2) and ~2 overrides forget it, so changed habits win. Learned rules auto-fill categories in receipts/quick-add/chat and are injected into Echo's prompt (getPromptHints, moneyChat.ts:939) at zero extra AI cost. The notebook lives on the phone + the user's own cloud sync (getSyncData/applySyncedLearning); chat text is never uploaded. It is entirely FREE for every tier — no gate, no quota (no PaywallModal import in EchoNotebook.tsx); the only tier-related behavior is that the rules feed the same metered Echo chat described above. ECHO REMEMBERS YOU (added 2026-07-28): a second, distinct layer in the SAME notebook store — durable free-text facts about the owner (goal / regular bill / worry / win / style / fact), shown under 'what echo remembers about you' alongside the learned shortcuts. Unlike the free-for-all learned rules, this memory is TIER-CAPPED (echoMemories: free 20 / basic 35 / pro 60 / premium 120 — free is deliberately generous, paid plans remember more). Facts are captured two ways: Echo auto-distills one when it learns something durable in chat (a [MEMORY] tag it emits, parsed like [ACTION], max 2/reply, source 'echo noticed'), and the owner can add/edit/pin/delete their own (source 'you told echo'). Every fact is visible and deletable; 'reset all' wipes both memories and rules. Only the short distilled fact is stored + synced (on-device + own cloud sync, never raw chat text); account-switch clears it. The capped set is injected into every Echo reply (getMemoryHints, MEMORY_PROMPT_LINES=15 pinned-first) so Echo 'never starts blank'. NO paywall modal — hitting the cap just shows an inline 'memory full — forget one or upgrade' note.

engine.howLimitCheckWorks: Every gate reads the ACTIVE tier's row in the single TIER_LIMITS table (src/constants/tiers.ts:51-92) through two pure helpers: canCreate(tier, key, currentCount) = currentCount < TIER_LIMITS[tier][key] (tiers.ts:116-118), and remainingOf() for display (tiers.ts:121-124). Infinity = unlimited (Pro/Premium count caps). The premium store exposes thin wrappers: count gates like canCreateWallet/Budget/Goal/SavingsAccount/SharedSub take the caller-supplied current count (premiumStore.ts:92-96); metered gates canScanReceipt()/canUseAI() first run resetXIfNeeded() then canCreate() against the stored counter (premiumStore.ts:99-117); capability gates hasCloudBackup/hasAskEcho/hasPhotoIcon just return the boolean from TIER_LIMITS (premiumStore.ts:120-122). Enforcement is 100% client-side — no server check; the paywall itself enforces nothing, it only reads FREE_TIER limits for its copy (PaywallModal.tsx:100-110). When billing is unconfigured, Continue calls applyTier() to unlock locally (PaywallModal.tsx:370-372).
engine.whatHappensAtLimit: Three behaviors, not one. (1) COUNT quota gates (wallets/budgets/savings/goals/subs) HARD-block: caller does if(!canCreateX(n)){ setPaywallVisible(true); return; } so the create is prevented and the paywall shown (Goals.tsx:810-813, SavingsTracker.tsx:224, BudgetPlanning.tsx:649). (2) METERED quota gates degrade gracefully, not block: out of scans falls back to free on-device OCR and STILL scans, paywalling only when out AND no local OCR exists (ReceiptScanner.tsx:336-340); out of AI credits silently falls back to the offline reader or returns null with no paywall (NoteEditor.tsx:465-483, spendingMirror.ts:168, checkinMessage.ts:29, reportNarrative.ts:40, intentEngine.ts:486). (3) CAPABILITY gates hard-block + paywall the whole feature (backup toggle AccountScreen.tsx:136/273; photo icons CommitmentForm.tsx:447, CategoryManager.tsx:90, Goals.tsx:1521). So: count + capability = hard block; scans/AI = soft degrade. Legacy over-cap users are grandfathered — blocked from creating MORE, never deleted (tiers.ts:110-118).
usageCountersTracked: tier + subscribedAt — persisted entitlement state, premiumStore.ts:29-30
wallets/budgets/savings/goals/shared-subs counts — NOT stored in premium store; live length passed by the caller's own domain store at check time (e.g. Goals.tsx:810, BudgetPlanning.tsx:649)
engine.howIncremented: incrementScanCount() does scanCount+1 (premiumStore.ts:52-55) and is called ONLY after a successful CLOUD scan — local OCR fallback never burns quota (ReceiptScanner.tsx:349-350, DebtTracking.tsx:2681/2763, CostManagement.tsx:333). incrementAiCalls() runs resetAiCallsIfNeeded() then aiCallsCount+1 (premiumStore.ts:71-75), called after each real AI call (moneyChat.ts:1030/1100, playbookAI.ts:628/729/777, queryEngine.ts:397, intentEngine.ts:507, collectzParser.ts:111). Count gates have no increment step — they read live object counts, so creating/deleting a wallet/goal/etc. moves the number naturally.
engine.whenCountersReset: Metered counters reset monthly and LAZILY (no timer). resetScanCountIfNeeded() / resetAiCallsIfNeeded() (premiumStore.ts:57-69, 77-89) compare the stored reset date against startOfMonth(now); if it is an earlier month or invalid, they zero the count and stamp the current month start. They fire at the top of every read gate (canScanReceipt :99-102, canUseAI :109-112, getRemainingScans :104-107, getRemainingAiCalls :114-117) and inside incrementAiCalls, so the reset happens on the first access in a new calendar month. onRehydrateStorage backfills a valid reset date on load (premiumStore.ts:143-144). Count gates (wallets etc.) never reset — they track real objects.
engine.capabilityGatesVsQuotaGates: CAPABILITY gates = a feature entirely locked until a tier that owns it, expressed as booleans in TIER_LIMITS: cloudBackup, askEchoPerScreen, photoCategoryIcons, plus exportData/googleDocsSync (tiers.ts:44-48). Free tier has these OFF (tiers.ts:59-60); there is no 'X free' — the whole feature is unavailable, surfaced via hasCloudBackup/hasAskEcho/hasPhotoIcon (premiumStore.ts:120-122). In the paywall these carry freeLimit:0 (backup, PaywallModal.tsx:108) which suppresses the quota trigger line (PaywallModal.tsx:334-336). QUOTA gates = X free then pay: numeric caps in TIER_LIMITS — count caps (maxWallets/Budgets/Savings/Goals/SharedSubs, unlimited=Infinity at Pro+) and metered caps (maxScansPerMonth, maxAiCallsPerMonth, which stay FINITE even on Premium because each costs real compute, tiers.ts:9-12). Their paywall copy shows 'used {currentUsage} of {freeLimit} {unit}' (PaywallModal.tsx:100-110, 337-344).
engine.hardVsSoftGate: HARD gate (action blocked): all COUNT quota gates and all CAPABILITY gates — caller checks the boolean, shows the paywall, and returns without doing the action (Goals.tsx:810-813, SavingsTracker.tsx:224, BudgetPlanning.tsx:649, AccountScreen.tsx:136/273, CommitmentForm.tsx:447). SOFT gate (action proceeds, degraded): the two COST-METERED resources. Scans fall back to free on-device OCR and still complete, paywalling only when no local OCR is available (ReceiptScanner.tsx:336-340). AI silently drops to the offline/rule-based path or returns null with no paywall at all (NoteEditor.tsx:465-483, spendingMirror.ts:168, checkinMessage.ts:29, reportNarrative.ts:40, queryEngine.ts:390, intentEngine.ts:486). So 'out of AI/scans' rarely blocks the user — it just quietly stops spending cloud tokens.

items.topic: Which store bills the customer — Apple or Google, never us
items.detail: Potraces never touches the customer's card. On iPhones the charge goes to the customer's Apple ID / App Store account; on Android it goes to their Google Play account. The paywall automatically shows the right store's name per device (src/components/common/PaywallModal.tsx:243-247; the labels 'Apple ID'/'App Store account' vs 'Google Play account'/'Google Play subscriptions' at src/i18n/en.ts:2904-2907). The billing engine underneath is a service called RevenueCat that sits between us and the two stores (src/services/billing.ts:1-14).

It asks the store 'has this person already paid?' and, if so, re-activates their plan on the current device — useful after reinstalling or switching phones (src/services/billing.ts:77-82). Apple requires this button to be reachable OUTSIDE the paywall, so it appears in three places: the paywall itself, the Settings subscription card, and the My Plan screen (src/components/common/PaywallModal.tsx:375-382, src/components/settings/SubscriptionCard.tsx:54-62, src/screens/shared/MyPlan.tsx:82-90). While billing is dormant it does nothing (safe no-op).

Three paid tiers (all in Malaysian Ringgit): Basic RM7.99/mo (monthly only), Pro RM14/mo or RM120/yr (works out to ~RM10/mo, badged −28%), Premium RM25/mo or RM200/yr (~RM16.67/mo, badged −33%) — src/components/common/PaywallModal.tsx:139-161. Basic is the deliberately-pushed 'hero': pre-selected and tagged BEST VALUE (PaywallModal.tsx:319-321, 455-459).

A monthly/yearly toggle sits at the top of the plan cards (src/components/common/PaywallModal.tsx:447-453). Important quirk: Basic has NO yearly option — it's monthly-only, and picking 'yearly' still shows it at RM7.99/mo (src/components/common/PaywallModal.tsx:144, src/services/billingMap.ts:18-22). Only Pro and Premium have a real yearly discount. Monthly is shown first on purpose, so the RM7.99→RM14 gap stays visible and yearly Pro (~RM10/mo) doesn't undercut Basic (PaywallModal.tsx:319-320).

items.topic: The discount claims are kept honest
items.detail: Every struck-through 'was' price on the yearly cards is a real 12× the monthly price, so the '−28%'/'−33%' savings badges aren't inflated (comment at src/components/common/PaywallModal.tsx:116-117; e.g. Pro yearly shows was RM14 → RM10, PaywallModal.tsx:151).

Cancelling is done in the store (App Store / Google Play), and must be at least 24 hours before the period ends to avoid the next charge (src/i18n/en.ts:2897, 2902-2903). Cancelling stops FUTURE charges but the plan stays active until the end of the already-paid period — it doesn't cut them off immediately (src/i18n/en.ts:2898). The subscription auto-renews at the shown price until cancelled (en.ts:2895).

items.topic: The in-app 'Cancel subscription' button is not a real store cancel
items.detail: The 'Cancel subscription' link in Settings just flips the account back to Free locally and shows a toast (src/components/settings/SubscriptionCard.tsx:73-93 calling unsubscribe in src/store/premiumStore.ts:46-50). It does NOT cancel the actual store subscription — the customer must still do that in Apple/Google. Once real billing is live, RevenueCat re-syncs the true entitlement on next launch (src/services/billing.ts:41-51), so a locally 'cancelled' but still-store-active user would get their tier restored. Worth aligning this UX before launch.

This is the single biggest reason to pay. On the FREE tier data lives on that one phone only — the app literally warns 'Saved on this phone only — lose it, lose everything' (src/i18n/en.ts:396-397, cloudBackup:false at src/constants/tiers.ts:60). Every PAID tier (Basic and up) turns on cloud backup so money data survives across devices (tiers.ts:70,80,90; paywall promise 'your tracks, never lost' at src/components/common/PaywallModal.tsx:507-512, src/i18n/en.ts:2859-2860). If someone downgrades or their subscription lapses, syncing is automatically switched off so they can't keep backing up for free (src/store/premiumStore.ts:9-20).

The ladder is Free → Basic → Pro → Premium; the My Plan screen offers one step up at a time and Premium has nowhere higher to go (src/screens/shared/MyPlan.tsx:31-35). If a customer somehow holds overlapping entitlements, the app always grants the HIGHEST one they're entitled to, so a legacy/overlapping purchase can never accidentally downgrade a Premium user (src/services/billingMap.ts:43-49).

items.topic: Downgrading never deletes a customer's data (grandfathering)
items.detail: If someone drops to a lower tier while over the new limit (e.g. they had 6 wallets, the new cap is fewer), nothing is deleted — they simply can't create MORE until they're back under the cap (src/constants/tiers.ts:110-118, comment at src/store/premiumStore.ts:22-25). Safe, non-destructive downgrades.

Free tier caps: 7 wallets, 6 budgets, 3 savings accounts, 3 goals, 3 shared subscriptions, 15 receipt scans/month, 30 AI chat calls/month, and NO cloud backup, NO 'Ask Echo' AI on screens, NO photo category icons (src/constants/tiers.ts:60-71). The scan and AI monthly counters reset at the start of each calendar month (src/store/premiumStore.ts:57-89).

items.topic: Scans and AI stay capped even on Premium (margin protection)
items.detail: Unlike wallets/budgets/goals — which become unlimited from Pro upward because they're cheap to give — receipt scans and AI calls always have a ceiling, even on Premium (Premium = 300 scans + 1500 AI calls/month), because each one costs us real compute money (src/constants/tiers.ts:10-12, 87). This is a deliberate cost-control decision, not an oversight.

items.topic: Once live, plans stay in sync automatically
items.detail: When billing is turned on, the app listens to RevenueCat and keeps the customer's tier matched to their true, current entitlement across renewals, expiries, refunds, and other devices — no manual reconciliation needed (src/services/billing.ts:34-52). If a refund or expiry happens, the app downgrades them automatically.

gaps.planSummary: The monetization plan (docs/MONETIZATION_AND_PRICING.md, "FEATURE-GATING LOCKED 2026-07-18") defines a 4-tier model (free / Basic RM7.99 / Pro RM14 / Premium RM25) with two gate families: COUNT caps that go unlimited at Pro+ (wallets, wallets-per-type, budgets, savings, goals, shared subs) and COST-METERED caps that stay finite even at Premium (Echo AI calls/mo, receipt scans/mo, statement/CSV imports/mo), plus three capability gates off on free (Ask-Echo-per-screen, cloud backup, photo category icons) and a business/storefront + Premium-payments layer. Implementation status: the personal count caps and the Echo/scan/photo/backup/Ask-Echo gates are all BUILT and wired to src/constants/tiers.ts (TIER_LIMITS), matching the plan numbers. NOT built to plan: the statement/CSV import ladder (only a flat server-side free cap exists, no paid ladder, no client paywall), all seller/storefront paid perks (badge removal, templates, analytics, AI business insights — paywall copy only or unbuilt), the Premium payment tools (Tap-to-Pay, QR-accept — acknowledged future), and the planned invisible voice/STT minute metering. Meta-gap: no tier actually charges — RevenueCat is scaffolded but dormant (local flag flip). Code also ships two limits NOT in the pricing doc (chatSavedBubbles history lock; Collectz/Playbooks caps).
